meta.title: CivicPulse — Run the 22 all night
meta.description: Rally deck for CivicPulse's Eastside night-bus campaign in Millbrook: 6,800 night workers walk home after the last 22 bus, a £1.9M all-night service would fix it, and the council votes on 14 January 2027.

slides.eyebrow: CivicPulse · Eastside night-bus campaign · Millbrook, winter 2026
slides.heading: Our shifts end after midnight. The 22 should too.
slides.lead: A people's campaign for an all-night bus on Route 22.
slides.notes: Read the line slowly. Let the room repeat it before you go on.

slides.heading: At 23:52 the last 22 leaves, and the night shift walks
slides.lead: Past the hospital, the depot and the retail park, in the dark.

slides.heading: Picture a lit 22 every 30 minutes, all night
slides.lead: From St Anne's Hospital to Harbour Depot, door to door by 01:00.

slides.imageAlt: A cream Route 22 bus with warm amber windows drives through the night on a cobalt street.

slides.heading: The council calls it too costly; it costs less than one junction
slides.left:
Night buses run empty.
£1.9M a year is unaffordable.
Taxis fill the gap.
slides.right:
Our survey: 2,100 riders a night.
£1.9M is a third of the A61 junction.
A taxi home costs £18.
slides.notes: Do not attack councillors by name. Attack the number; the facts do the work.

slides.quote: I finish at half twelve and walk forty minutes past the retail park. I carry my keys between my fingers every night.
slides.by: Grace Okafor, night nurse at St Anne's Hospital

slides.heading: Three moves get the 22 running all night by summer
